Welcome

  • Features
  • Examples
  • Resources

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. The “Learn more” button above demonstrates smooth transitions and proper visual feedback.

Try using the Tab key to navigate through all interactive elements.

Accessible Form

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

Resources

Want to learn more about web accessibility and semantic HTML? Check out these resources:

  • WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference (opens in new tab)
  • HTML Living Standard (opens in new tab)
  • A11y 101 (opens in new tab)

content.text:
I've fixed `0.html`; the edits are in place, but nothing has been tested in a browser, since this session couldn't run the commands needed for that.

## What was broken

- **Curly quotes in the Examples section.** Every attribute there used `”` instead of `"`, so the classes, ids, inline styles and the `onclick` handler didn't parse. The cards were unstyled and the labels weren't linked to their inputs. These are now straight quotes; the `“Learn more”` in the body text is left alone.
- **CSP blocked the script.** `default-src 'none'` with no `script-src` meant the inline script never ran. I added `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` and replaced the `onclick` attribute with `addEventListener`.
- **Form submission was blocked.** `form-action 'none'` stops the form submitting, so I added a submit handler that shows a "demo, nothing was sent" message in a `role="status"` paragraph.

## Other improvements

- **Inline styles moved to CSS.** The form and live-region styles are now `.field`, `label`, `input`/`textarea` and `.live-region` rules.
- **Required marker.** The `aria-label` on a `<span>` is replaced with a hidden-from-screen-readers `*` plus visually hidden "(required)" text, and the email input has `autocomplete="email"`.
- **Input fonts.** Inputs use `font: inherit`, so they match the page font and size.
- **Live region messages.** They now cycle in order instead of being random, because a repeated message would not be announced again.
- **Anchor offsets.** `scroll-margin-top` now applies to any element with an id, since the nav links target the `<h2>` headings rather than the sections.
- **Back to top.** The footer link points to `#top` instead of `#main`.

## Decision for you

`script-src 'unsafe-inline'` is looser than I'd like. I wanted to pin the script with a SHA-256 hash instead, but the command to compute it was denied. To tighten it, run this and replace `'unsafe-inline'` in `script-src` with `'sha256-<output>'`:

```sh
perl -0777 -ne 'print $1 if /<script>(.*?)<\/script>/s' 0.html | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | base64
```

The catch is that the hash has to be regenerated every time the script changes.

No backup of the original was made, because that command was denied too.

## Decision for you

`script-src 'unsafe-inline'` is looser than I'd like. I wanted to pin the script with a SHA-256 hash instead, but the command to compute it was denied. To tighten it, run this and replace `'unsafe-inline'` in `script-src` with `'sha256-<output>'`:

```sh
perl -0777 -ne 'print $1 if /<script>(.*?)<\/script>/s' 0.html | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | base64
```

The catch is that the hash has to be regenerated every time the script changes.

No backup of the original was made, because that command was denied too.
